newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt led lower by another Brazil stock plunge.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt led lower by another Brazil stock plunge.

text.p: Emerging market debt turned lower Thursday afternoon, prompted by steep losses in the Sao Paolo stock market and a late-day slump in U.S. Treasuries, traders said.

"It's 100 percent dealer trades," one Brady bond trader said of the late selloff. "Mexico, Argentina and Brazil are the hardest hit, and Venezuela, Eastern Europe and some of the exotics are holding up better."
Brazil "C" bonds slipped 7/8 to 82-5/8 as stock prices plunged, traders said.
Other major Latin America instruments followed suit, with Argentina FRBs off 3/8 at 94 and Mexico pars down 1/2 at 80.

Sao Paolo's 47-stock Bovespa index tumbled more than 7.0 percent by 1415 EDT/1815 GMT. Its volatility this week -- falling about 9.0 percent on Tuesday, then rebounding about 7.0 percent on Wednesday -- has made investors nervous.
The drop in Brazil debt prices followed Wednesday's strong gains, which were keyed by the country's insistance Asian currency troubles would not lead to speculation against the real.

Political turmoil continued to unfold in Peru, where President Alberto Fujimori's cabinet suffered another resignation. Defense Minister Gen. Tomas Castillo Meza quit over rights abuses by the security forces, according to government sources.
More broadly, Ecuador PDIs dipped 7/8 to 67-1/2, Bulgaria IABs rose 1/2 to 74-7/8 and Venezuela FLIRBs fell 1/2 to 92-3/4.
